paragraphs: Friend, here's the lesson. Pride sets itself up against the LORD, and it always ends empty. Moab bragged and bragged, and the LORD said "His boasting is as empty as his deeds" (Jer 48:30). Nobody wins an argument with the One who made them, and I say that as a stamper who once tried to out-brag his own oven.

But look at who is doing the crying. The LORD says, "Therefore I will wail for Moab" (Jer 48:31), and His heart "laments like a flute for Moab" (Jer 48:36). Judgment here does not come from a God who enjoys it. I think that's the part to hold onto, friend: the One who brings pride low is the same One who grieves over it.

And then comes the little word that gets me every time. "Yet in the latter days I will restore Moab from captivity," declares the LORD (Jer 48:47). Pride can bring a nation low, but it doesn't get the last word, because the LORD does. So bring your pride to Him before it breaks, and know that He restores what He has brought low. The teaching isn't over, either, so stay in the Word.
